name: United Arab Emirates
flagName: Flag of the United Arab Emirates
summary: Green, white and black horizontal bands with a vertical red band at the hoist, in the Pan-Arab colours. Designed by a 19-year-old, it was raised when the federation was formed on 2 December 1971.
origin: Before the union, the Trucial States used red-and-white flags. Ahead of federation, a public competition was held; Abdullah Mohammed Al Maainah, then 19, submitted the winning design among more than 1,000 entries.
The flag was first raised by Sheikh Zayed bin Sultan Al Nahyan, the first President, at Union House in Dubai on 2 December 1971.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: From the flags of the individual emirates; commonly linked to courage and sacrifice.

colors.name: Green
colors.meaning: Commonly linked to fertility and prosperity.

colors.name: White
colors.meaning: Commonly linked to neutrality and peace.

colors.name: Black
colors.meaning: Commonly linked to the defeat of enemies, or the oil wealth of the country.

facts: UAE Flag Day is 3 November, marking the accession of President Khalifa bin Zayed in 2004.
The colours come from a line of Arab poetry by Safi al-Din al-Hilli, often quoted as their meaning: white deeds, black battles, green pastures, red swords.
Each of the seven emirates also has its own flag, most red with white.
clues: A vertical red band at the hoist, with green, white and black horizontal bands.
Designed by a 19-year-old in a competition for a new federation in 1971.
Its seven member states each keep their own flags.
